If you sell digital products, these are 3 legal documents you need to know about, and most sellers completely overlook number 3 👀 1️⃣ Digital Product Purchase Agreement This can establish the terms of the purchase, including restrictions on sharing or reselling your digital product and other important purchase terms. 2️⃣ Website/Store Terms & Conditions Your Terms & Conditions establish the rules for your online business and can address things like refunds, intellectual property, and limitations of liability. 3️⃣ Content Usage License If a brand or client pays to use your videos, templates, graphics, courses, or other content, a content usage license can clearly define how they can use it, where, for how long, and what happens if they go beyond those rights. Your creativity is an asset. Treat it like one. 💅🏾 And no, you don't necessarily need to spend hundreds on legal fees just to get foundational documents in place. I went and found five digital products that have each sold over a thousand copies, so you don't have to. They're all on screen so you can go and check the numbers for yourself. Number four is the one nobody expected, including me, so stay for that one. Number one is a brush set at $5 and it's done 23,500 sales. It's not a course, it's not a bundle, it's just brushes. Number two is a travel planner built inside Notion at $20, and that's done over 2,900 sales. There are nearly 20,000 Notion templates on that platform, and it beat all of them because it's about travelling and not about productivity. Number three is a teaching resource at $25 with 2,900 sales, and it was obviously made for teachers by somebody who used to be a teacher — nobody else would have known exactly how to build it that way. Number four is the one I did not expect: a drawing course at $100 with 1,800 sales. A hundred dollars, for foundations in drawing with brushes and charcoal. Nearly 2,000 people have paid for it. That's insane. And number five is a freelance dashboard at $97 with 1,200 sales. Now look at what's in that list. There's no AI in it anywhere. No make money online, no productivity system. It's brushes, travel, teaching, drawing and freelancing — and every one of them is a specific person doing a specific thing. The prices run from $5 all the way up to $100. So there isn't one right price, just the right price for the person you pick. Stop asking what sells and start asking who you actually know something about, because that's the only thing these five have in common. #creatorsearchinsights What are digital products? They’re downloadable items people can buy and access online—like Canva templates, workbooks, guides, checklists, planners, funeral programs, graduation announcements, and media kits. You create the product, upload it to a selling platform, and the customer downloads it. No shipping. No boxes. No physical inventory. But here’s the truth: a digital product still needs to solve a real problem.
